title: Trump Announces Ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico From White House Grounds
detail: President Trump said Friday, September 18, 2026, that he is 'banning' CNN, MS NOW (formerly MSNBC) and Politico from the White House, accusing the outlets of constantly reporting 'FICTION and LIES' about his administration. The ban took effect the following morning, Saturday, September 19: a reporter and cameraman from MS NOW were denied entry to White House grounds and had their press badges confiscated by Secret Service at a security gate outside the West Wing, and CNN and Politico staff reported similar denials. All three outlets said they would pursue legal action, arguing the move violates the First Amendment; the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals has previously held that once the White House opens press facilities to journalists, it cannot deny access arbitrarily or without due process. The ban is the most sweeping White House press restriction of Trump's second term and follows earlier disputes over the Associated Press's access after it declined to adopt the administration's 'Gulf of America' naming.

media.caption: Trump announced he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House; reporters from the outlets were denied entry the next morning

title: Trump Signs Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act Into Law
detail: President Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law Friday, September 18, 2026, honoring the late South Carolina senator who died in July of a torn aorta shortly after returning from a trip to Ukraine, where he had championed tougher sanctions on Moscow. The bill cleared the Senate 86-11 on August 7 and the House 262-159 on September 16 before reaching Trump's desk. It gives the president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries that buy Russian crude oil or natural gas or otherwise help Russia evade sanctions — a provision aimed chiefly at China and India, the two largest remaining buyers of Russian energy — while also targeting Russian officials, financial institutions, defense-related networks and the 'shadow fleet' of tankers used to move sanctioned oil, and extending the Iran Sanctions Act for five years. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed the law as an important tool to pressure Russia toward peace.

media.caption: Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil and gas

title: Trump Extends $100,000 H-1B Visa Fee Proclamation Through September 2027
detail: President Trump signed a proclamation Friday, September 18, 2026, extending his $100,000 fee requirement on certain new H-1B petitions for another year, through September 21, 2027, as his administration appeals a Massachusetts federal court ruling that struck down the fee in June 2026 as an unlawful tax rather than a valid immigration restriction. The original proclamation, signed September 19, 2025, imposed the fee on H-1B petitions for beneficiaries outside the US without a valid visa, effective September 21, 2025; more than 700 petitions have included the payment despite the court order currently blocking enforcement. Trump also issued a separate order the same day directing officials to weigh 'recent or planned layoffs' of US workers when reviewing H-1B employer applications, part of his broader push to permanently raise the standard H-1B fee from the $2,000-$5,000 range to at least $100,000.

media.caption: USCIS guidance on the $100,000 H-1B petition fee, which Trump extended through September 2027 despite a court order currently blocking its enforcement
